articles.title: Araghchi warns foreign military presence fuels tensions
articles.description: TEHRAN, Nov. 26 (MNA) – Iran and South Korea discussed bilateral ties and regional developments, as Tehran warned that foreign military forces in the region could heighten tensions and widen conflicts.

summary.headline: Iran warns South Korea that foreign military presence increases regional tensions
summary.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi spoke by telephone with South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun to discuss bilateral ties and regional developments. According to state-affiliated Mehr News, Araghchi stated that foreign military deployments in the region exacerbate tensions and widen conflicts. Cho Hyun reaffirmed South Korea's commitment to regional stability, stating Seoul has no intention of intervening in the war or deploying troops.
key_points: [12:02 UTC, Mehr News] Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun held a telephone conversation.
[12:02 UTC, Mehr News] Araghchi warned that foreign military presence in the region fuels tensions and expands conflicts.
[12:02 UTC, Mehr News] Cho Hyun stated that South Korea has no intention of intervening in the war or deploying troops to the region.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit sea mines near Oman’s Khasab, Tasnim reports
articles.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit sea mines near Oman’s Khasab, Tasnim reports Two tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting sea mines north of Oman’s Khasab port while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz through what the Revolutionary Guards’ navy called an unauthorised route, the Guards said in a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim news agency on Thursday.
